newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe 1996 gold output down on 1995.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe 1996 gold output down on 1995.

text.p: Zimbabwe gold output slipped to 23.7 tonnes in 1996 from 24.3 tonnes the previous year, largely due to production problems at the country's major gold mines, an industry official said on Thursday.
Chamber of Mines chief executive Derek Bain said 1996's production was down on forecasts of just over 25 tonnes, which would have been the highest output in 80 years.
Zimbabwe's highest gold production on record was in 1916 when 27 tonnes of the metal were mined.

"We produced 23.7 tonnes (in 1996) valued at just over Z$3 billion (US$277 million). We were looking at 25.3 tonnes and we were on track to meet those forecasts up until June when production started dropping," Bain said.
"We don't know for certain why production dropped but some of our major mines had production problems," he told Reuters.

Bain declined to say which mines had experienced problems but in August one of the biggest, Rio Tinto Zimbabwe, said it anticipated a drop in output from its Cam Dump as it reverted to a high throughput of generally low grade material.

In its results for the half-year ended June 30, Rio Tinto also reported difficulties at its Empress refinery, which toll-refines material from Botswana, saying it was experiencing disruptions caused by commissioning work.
On Thursday, Bain said the chamber had expected gold miners to increase production to improve revenues in view of a depressed international gold price, but that had not happened.
He said the squeeze on revenues was exacerbated by high input costs on the back of energy and fuel price hikes, but the depreciation of the Zimbabwean dollar against major currencies had offset this.

Bain declined to comment on prospects for the industry -- one of Zimbabwe's top foreign exchange earners -- in the current year, save to say he hoped miners would expand to increase output in the face of a declining bullion price in the New Year.
The gold price has fallen by some US$15 since the beginning of the year. It was fixed in London at $356.50 an ounce on Thursday afternoon.
Zimbabwe is Africa's third largest gold producer after South Africa and Ghana.
Bain said gold and base mineral exports earned Zimbabwe Z$7.3 billion (US$674 million) in 1996 compared to Z$6.7 billion (US$619 million) in 1995.
